newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Branson lifts off on round-world balloon bid.
newsitem.headline: Branson lifts off on round-world balloon bid.

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson and two co-pilots soared skywards from the Moroccan city of Marrakesh at 11.19 a.m. (1119 GMT) on Tuesday to try to be the first to fly around the world by balloon.

Watched by Branson's wife, Joan, and children Holly, 15, and Sam, 11, the 1.1 million cubic foot (30,000 cubic metre) helium and hot air balloon soared into a sunlit sky near the snow-capped Atlas Mountains. Branson could be seen waving through the capsule window.
Just before take-off and embracing his family, Branson said: "We are definitely coming back to Marrakesh next year to celebrate this event. We are now going on a great adventure. I am confident."

Flying eastward in the southern jet stream, Branson, Per Linstrand, 48, and Alex Ritchie, 50, will head at around 30,000 feet (9,150 metres) across North Africa, Saudi Arabia and India, the South China Sea, the Pacific, the United States and then to Britain.

Branson, 46, head of the Virgin group of companies, expects the trip to take between 14 and 21 days, ending in Oxfordshire. One of the original co-pilots, Rory McCarthy, had to pull out because of suspected pneumonia and was replaced by standby co-pilot Ritchie.
